correctness.rationale: Given the explicitly cited published Laface–Ugaglia criterion (generation iff every positively spanning three-ray A satisfies I_X not contained in P_A^2), the sparse-interval lemma is proved by unimodular coordinates. If v,w adjacent, dual u=(-1,0) gives a lattice binomial with A-degree one on one side. With one intermediate ray q, choose v=(1,0),q=(0,1),w=(-1,m); u=(sign(a),0) for third selected ray z=(a,b) similarly has an A-degree-one side. Therefore obstruction requires >=2 intermediary rays in each of three disjoint arcs, r>=9. For witness nine rays listed in pinned RESULT, independent exact integer checks verify every cyclic adjacent determinant=1 and triple selected at positions 2,5,8 has determinants=3, sum zero and two rays per arc. For arbitrary character u=(a,b), triple pairings (b,b-3a,3a-2b) sum zero and are congruent mod3; hence both monomial A-degrees >=2, proving I_X subset P_A^2 for all u. The existence of published criterion is relied upon, not re-proved; primary full text was unavailable.

value.rationale: The exact minimal Picard/ray complexity for failure of degree-one Rees generation of a torus-point blow-up Cox ring is a natural, independently useful geometric threshold. The combinatorial sparse-interval obstruction applies uniformly to all smooth complete toric surfaces; the nine-ray fan shows the bound sharp rather than offering an unmotivated isolated example.

final_claim: Over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, for a smooth complete toric surface X with r rays, Cox(Bl_e X) is generated in Rees multiplicity one for every r<=8; r=9 is sharp via an explicit nine-ray smooth complete fan and an obstructing positively spanning triple with two intermediate rays in each interval.
limitations: Characteristic zero, algebraically closed field, smooth complete toric surfaces, torus identity blow-up only.
